newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher on awaited rebound.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher on awaited rebound.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Friday as the market attracted fresh buyers after the declines earlier in the week.
"This was a technical, logical and awaited rebound - prices were tempting at these yield levels," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 91-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 advanced $0.25 to 126.60.
Traders said investors had been waiting for the right moment to enter the market after its declines Thursday and Wednesday.
Despite the rebound, traders said that local trading volumes remained stubbornly thin, evidencing a continued lack of clear direction for the market.
The session's rebound was also largely thanks to gains in U.S. Treasuries, as opposed to any domestic news.
"A mild rebound in Treasury bonds sparked a larger than expected rally in Latin Bradies," said analysts at MMS International in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.38 percent from 6.48 percent.
